4. I have heard counsel for the parties and considered their respective submission besides examining the requisitioned record.
5. Claimants/respondents No.1 to 3 filed a petition under Section 166 of MV Act for grant of compensation of Rs.60 lacs on account of death of Balwinder Singh.

It was averred that after discharging his duties as Government teacher in the Government High School in Muradpura on 09.09.2013, Balwinder Singh was returning hhome on Activa scooter when a tractor trolley bearing registration No.PB No.PB-09-Q-8002 8002 being rashly driven by appellant No.1, hit the scooter resulting in his death.
Information nformation about the accident was immediately given to the police, but they did not register the FIR.
After inquiring into the complaint submitted by the widow to superior police officials, an FIR was eventually registered on 28.03.2015 under Sections 279 and 304-A 304 IPC.
Claim petition was contested by the appellants on the ground that no accident had taken place and a false FIR has been registered after an unexplained delay.

In Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and others, (2011) 4 SCC 693, Supreme Court has held that the registration of a criminal case proves the factum of the accident and the delay in itself cannot be a ground for rejection of the claim petition.

Perusal of the certificate (Ex.P7) issued by Amandeep Hospital shows that Balwinder Singh was found to be suffering from Cx- Cx spine injury and had a bed sore with septicemia, which was the cause of his death.
